messages:
sam_infra: Heads up — I see a spike in inter-region egress on yesterday's bill, ~$12k overnight. Dashboard shows large GETs pulling model artifacts from us-west-2 to nodes in eu-west-1. :eyes:

nora_sre: wait, why do we have GPU nodes starting in eu-west-1? we normally scale in us-west-2 for this fleet.

sam_infra: autoscaler scaled out the 'inference-gpu' pool after a sudden QPS increase. Looks like the autoscaler selected available capacity in eu-west-1 because our reserved commitments only cover specific instance SKUs in us-west-2. The pool had no allowed_zones constraint so it fell through to other regions.

liam_runtime: that would explain model pulls — our model cache is regional (S3 in us-west-2). New nodes boot and run the startup hook to sync weights with `rwd-model-fetch`. Cross-region downloads are billed as egress.

nora_sre: can you paste the autoscaler snippet?

sam_infra: sure — here's the scaledown policy block from the provisioning config that got applied:```yaml
provisioner: inference-gpu
min: 10
max: 120
autoZones: true # <-- relies on cloud to pick zones
allowed_zones: [] # accidentally left empty in the deploy
instanceTypes: [a100, v100]
fallback: allow-other-regions
```

nora_sre: oh yeah, `allowed_zones: []` + `fallback: allow-other-regions` is the smoking gun. Should be `allowed_zones: [us-west-2a, us-west-2b]` for the committed pool. :facepalm:

deploy-bot: [deploy] Provisioner inference-gpu updated by @ci-cd (commit 7f3b2) — autodeploy at 2026-03-16T03:12:01Z

tom_finance: rough numbers: cost explorer shows ~11.7k in cross-region egress plus ~1.1k in on-demand difference for eu-west launched nodes vs committed reserved rates. total ~12.8k for the window. This is a one-off but still large.

liam_runtime: logs from node startup show repeated fetches of the 12GB weight tarball:```
[2026-03-16T03:15:05Z] rwd-model-fetch: GET https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/rwd-models/ggml-large-v2.tar.gz range 0-52428800
[2026-03-16T03:15:10Z] rwd-model-fetch: GET https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/rwd-models/ggml-large-v2.tar.gz range 52428801-104857600
... repeated until full download
```

nora_sre: did the prewarm job fail? we should have a regional prewarm that populates cache before allowing scale-out.

sam_infra: prewarm job was healthy for us-west-2, but the autoscaler didn't honor `regionAffinity`. New nodes came up with cloud_region=eu-west-1 so prewarm job didn't run there.

liam_runtime: other gotchas: the model fetcher doesn't use multipart parallel copy across regions, so each new node did a full single-threaded download — expensive and slow.

nora_sre: mitigation steps we should do now: 1) set autoscaler to deny other regions for this fleet, 2) apply a temporary nodeSelector taint for eu nodes to block inference workloads, 3) trigger cache-warm in us-west-2-only pools, 4) revoke autoscale fallback until commit coverage verified.

sam_infra: I'm already applying a hotfix to the provisioner: patching `allowed_zones` to explicit us-west-2 zones and turning off `fallback: allow-other-regions`. Pushing in 2 mins.

deploy-bot: [deploy] Provisioner inference-gpu updated by sam_infra (commit b9c1d) — autodeploy at 2026-03-16T03:22:18Z

tom_finance: thanks. Can ops also add a cost alert for >$2k inter-region egress in 1h for inference fleets? want to catch these fast.

nora_sre: yes — I'll add a CloudWatch alert + internal pager for the next 48h while we monitor. Also adding a billing dashboard widget for per-provisioner inter-region egress.

liam_runtime: long-term we should: - replicate model store to eu regions for geo workloads OR - ensure `regionAffinity` + regional prewarm + cache-miss throttles exist. Also add a startup guard limiting parallel model fetches (jitter + concurrency limit).

sam_infra: note for postmortem: this was a combination of (a) an overly permissive `fallback` policy, (b) empty `allowed_zones` defaulting to global, and (c) no admission controls to prevent inference pods landing on non-warmed regions.

tom_finance: cc @finance if we need to invoice back to product teams. For now treat as infra incident charge.

nora_sre: I'll open an incident ticket + short RCA draft. tagging this thread. :white_check_mark:

sam_infra: thanks team. will follow up with the incident link and the commits.

liam_runtime: postmortem action items: `protect-provisioner-zones`, `prewarm-guard`, `egress-cost-alerts`, `startup-concurrency-limit`.

sam_infra: last note — we should also look at switching large model weights to a regional CDN or object replication to avoid repeated cross-region GETs in case of future multi-region bursts.

nora_sre: agreed. follow-up scheduled in infra-ops planning. :calendar:
